Check whether a matrix looks like RNA-seq raw counts

Source: R/13d-IsCountsMatrix.R
IsCountsMatrix.Rd

Determines whether a numeric matrix is likely to be a bulk/single-cell RNA-seq raw counts matrix. A matrix is accepted only if it is non-empty, finite, non-negative, integer-like in a sufficiently high proportion, and has a positive library size for every sample. Useful for validating input before running count-based downstream analyses.

Usage

IsCountsMatrix(
  x,
  verbose = TRUE,
  integer_tol = 1e-08,
  min_integer_fraction = 0.95
)

Arguments

x

Numeric matrix. Rows are genes, columns are samples.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print diagnostic statistics (fractions of non-negative, integer-like, and zero values, library sizes, and the reason for rejection) to the console. Default: TRUE.

integer_tol

Numeric in [0, 1]. Absolute tolerance used to decide whether a value is integer-like (abs(x - round(x)) <= integer_tol). Default: 1e-8.

min_integer_fraction

Numeric in [0, 1]. Minimum fraction of integer-like values required for the matrix to be considered counts. Default: 0.95.

Value

A single logical value: TRUE if x is likely a bulk counts matrix, FALSE otherwise.

Details

IsCountsMatrix() rejects a matrix for any of the following reasons:

  • the matrix is empty;

  • the matrix contains NA, NaN, or infinite values;

  • the matrix contains negative values;

  • the fraction of integer-like values is below min_integer_fraction;

  • at least one sample (column) has a library size (column sum) <= 0.

When verbose = TRUE, the reason for rejection (or diagnostic statistics on acceptance) is printed to the console.

Examples

# A typical bulk RNA-seq raw counts matrix (genes x samples)
counts <- matrix(
  c(100, 200, 300, 150, 250, 350),
  nrow = 3, ncol = 2,
  dimnames = list(c("GENE1", "GENE2", "GENE3"), c("Sample1", "Sample2"))
)
IsCountsMatrix(counts)
#> ✔ Result: TRUE; matrix is likely a counts matrix (integer fraction among non-zero 1.000000, density 1.000000)
#> [1] TRUE

# A log-normalized matrix is not counts
IsCountsMatrix(log1p(counts))
#> ℹ Result: FALSE; insufficient integer-like values among non-zero entries (integer fraction 0.000000 < threshold 0.950000)
#> [1] FALSE

# Matrices containing negative values are not counts
IsCountsMatrix(counts - 1000)
#> ℹ Result: FALSE; matrix contains negative values
#> [1] FALSE

# Inspect diagnostic statistics
IsCountsMatrix(counts, verbose = TRUE)
#> ✔ Result: TRUE; matrix is likely a counts matrix (integer fraction among non-zero 1.000000, density 1.000000)
#> [1] TRUE
